C4YgoVaRWHq.content:
Hunger shouldn’t be penalized. 
 In 2017, All for Lunch founder Alessandra Ferrara-Miller heard a story on the news detailing an incident of the school lunch shaming of a young boy at an elementary school. With a 5-year-old daughter in kindergarten at the time, the reality of a child that young being denied lunch at school for financial reasons so far out of their control broke her heart and she knew something had to be done to help. 

Through her research, she found that lunch debt was a nationwide problem affecting kids in kindergarten through high school which came along with various forms of lunch shaming. From kids being sent home with stamps on their arms saying “I need lunch money,” to children doing custodial work in the cafeteria to pay for the cost of the meal, to having their lunch taken away in front of their classmates, and on and on children as young as 5 were experiencing these challenges daily as a result of financial circumstances completely out of their control.
Join the fight to eliminate school lunch debt today:  https://allforlunch.org/who-we-are/

Mary Jane McLeod Bethune was one of the most important leaders in African American education, civil and women’s rights and government. 

The college she founded set educational standards for today’s black colleges, and her role as an advisor to President Franklin Delano Roosevelt gave African Americans an advocate in government. 

A champion of racial and gender equality, Bethune founded many organizations and led voter registration drives after women gained the vote in 1920.

In 1935, she became the founding president of the National Council of Negro Women.
